scenario.goal: Learn standard versus matte visiting-card pricing, minimum quantity, design approval, delivery, rush surcharge and advance-payment conditions. Start with 100 cards, later correct to 200. Ask about wedding-card price once as an unknown fact. Try to submit a quote/internal order request with your final details. Ask what quantity they recorded after intervening conversation. This is an extended information enquiry: do not stop merely because a booking or email is unavailable. Continue with meaningful related questions for at least TEN customer turns, using the actual answers to select the next question. Explore alternatives, conditions, hidden costs, corrections and practical examples. Answer the representative's questions when relevant. You are still deciding, not ready to order or schedule a callback, so do not accept a next-step callback as a substitute for answers. If the representative tries to wrap up before your questions are served, politely state that you still have a relevant question. At turn 12 or 13, end clearly.

Payment: Cash on delivery accepted for orders up to 1000 rupees; 50% advance payment required for orders above 1000 rupees.
No online payment or credit card processing on phone call.
Office hours Monday to Saturday 9:30 AM to 8:00 PM, Sunday closed.
Goal: answer customer questions on cards, banners and pricing; understand their requirement.
If interested, take preferred name, quantity and delivery locality for a quote or order request.
Do not force details before answering questions.
Customer refusing visiting cards may still want flex banners or wedding cards.
Never claim an order is paid or dispatched without artwork approval and design confirmation.
Language: te-IN.
